expectations.text: Recommends a defensible event share for Brightforge without describing that share as an industry norm.
expectations.evidence: The answer gives a concrete recommendation — 'Defend a barbell: events near the top of the 50-60% band, paired with enablement' — and grounds it in Brightforge-specific facts (enterprise six-figure deals, security architect + platform lead dual sign-off) rather than in a benchmark. It explicitly refuses the norm framing throughout: opens with 'CFO wrong to call 15% "industry norm" — no such norm exists,' tags every weight as '(self-set starting point, adjust freely)' / '(self-set methodology, not a published figure)' including in the comparison table, and when it does cite the one real survey

expectations.text: Recommends a defensible event share for Brightforge without describing that share as an industry norm.
expectations.evidence: A specific share is recommended: "Target 25–30% ($105K–$126K), not 40% ($168K), pending a portfolio audit," and it is partly defended on Brightforge-specific grounds — 80/20 concentration audit of the current event list, cost-per-qualified-meeting/cost-per-opportunity scoreboard, and the observation that 15% ($63K) cannot fund two credible mid-tier conferences. It also explicitly rejects norm-matching as the test: "The right question isn't 'does 40% match a generic percentage.'" However, the recommended band is substantially anchored to a stated peer benchmark rather than Brightforge's own eco
